page: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading (2 threads per core). Cache allocation comprises 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The instance delivers 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio typical of memory-intensive cloud architectures. The configuration contains 0 dedicated GPUs and provides no bundled local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent data and operating system disks rely completely on remote attached block storage. Additionally, the instance is provisioned with 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In synthetic computing benchmarks, the E4_v4 delivers modest processing output, reflecting its two-physical-core constraint. Stress-ng returned a single-core score of 1,409.99 and a multi-core score of 3,698.58, both ranking in the weak tier. Geekbench testing mirrors this profile with a single-core score of 1,226.0 (average) and a multi-core score of 2,742.0 (weak). PassMark CPU overall reached 4,339.65. Uncached memory bandwidth scored 23.02 GB/sec for large-block reads and 18.0 GB/sec for large-block writes, positioning uncached memory throughput in the lower percentiles despite an average overall PassMark memory score of 2,211.77.

Application and domain-specific benchmarks show 3.56 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 3.79 GB/sec. Large language model inference utilizing a small 135M model achieved 224.56 prompt processing tokens per second and 62.24 generation tokens per second. Bzip3 single-threaded decompression scored in the average bracket at 9.19 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded decompression reached 17.34 GB/sec.

Microsoft Azure E4_v4 trades raw CPU parallelism for an expanded memory footprint. Cost efficiency is driven by workloads requiring higher RAM density per core without requiring high continuous compute throughput. Because of its 32.0 GB memory capacity paired with moderate CPU performance and lack of local scratch disks, this instance is suited for mid-sized relational database hosting, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise web backends, and lightweight data ingestion tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V, featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU), and no bundled local storage or GPUs. It incorporates hardware flags such as AVX-512, AES, and FMA. Benchmark evaluations reflect an architecture tailored for memory density over raw compute: single-core performance ranks average to weak (Geekbench single-core 1,226.0; stress-ng single-core 1,409.99), while multi-threaded capacity reflects the physical dual-core limit (Geekbench multi-core 2,742.0). Redis operations hit 3.56 million ops/sec, and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 23.02 GB/sec. The E4_v4 offers solid qualitative resource efficiency for memory-centric deployments, serving workloads such as mid-sized in-memory caches, relational databases, business intelligence services, and general enterprise applications.
